sections.h2: What makes Highlands County property tax different?
sections.html:
Highlands County is a large, mostly rural county, and that shapes how its tax roll works. The property appraiser says the county covers about 1,029 square miles of land, roughly 658,000 acres, with around 113,000 parcels, 60,000 buildings, 6,000 business accounts and 10,000 tangible personal property accounts on mobile homes.

Farmland is a big piece of that roll: about 75,000 acres of citrus, 275,000 acres of pasture and thousands of acres of cropland. The office also administers over 24,000 homestead exemptions. The tax collector serves the county from locations in Sebring and Avon Park, and the Highlands County Tax Collector posts the payment and deadline pages used below.

sections.h2: When is Highlands County property tax due?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed by October 31, collection begins in November, and the full amount is due by March 31. Anything unpaid or not postmarked by March 31 is delinquent on April 1, when interest and fees begin.

The appraiser's FAQ puts the early payment discounts at 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February. It adds that Highlands taxes are paid in arrears for the calendar year, January 1 to December 31, which matters at a closing because the seller owes part of a year that the buyer will be billed for.

  • Installment plan: apply by April 30 for the next tax year; payments fall in June (6% discount), September (4.5%), December (3%) and March (final, no discount).
  • Missed first payment: an account without the first installment by July 31 is removed from the plan and gets a full bill in October.
  • Homestead deferral: the county tax collector lists January 31 as its filing deadline for the deferral program.

sections.h2: What dates should a Highlands County owner mark?
sections.html:
The county's calendar runs from the January 1 valuation through the April 1 delinquency, with a handful of deadlines that catch sellers off guard.

In May, delinquent real estate accounts are advertised three times in a local newspaper, and delinquent tangible personal property accounts once.

sections.h2: How do homestead and agricultural classification work in Highlands County?
sections.html:
New homestead exemptions must be filed with the Highlands County Property Appraiser by March 1. The appraiser says the exemption is free to anyone who qualifies, and that it can be handled in minutes at the office or at visits to municipal sites around the county.

The office warns that new owners sometimes receive mailings offering a reduction in taxable value for a fee. It says such offers amount to the savings the homestead exemption already gives, and that the paid service is generally just information on how to apply.

Agricultural land follows a different rule. An application must be filed with the appraiser before March 1 of the tax year, and only land used in good faith for commercial agriculture qualifies. Once granted, the classification renews each year. A dwelling on the parcel does not disqualify the land, though the home site is assessed at just value. Citrus is valued by variety, and the office adjusts assessments when disease or freeze damage affects production, and it avoids entering groves because of disease concerns.

sections.h2: How can a Highlands County owner challenge a value or exemption?
sections.html:
Petition the Value Adjustment Board before the deadline printed on the TRIM notice, with a notarized petition and a $50 filing fee per parcel. The board has three county commissioners and two school board members, and it usually appoints special masters who are independent of the appraiser's office to hear cases.

  • For a value dispute, bring sales of comparable properties from the prior year, before January 1, or an appraisal.
  • For an exemption denial, show you qualified as of January 1.
  • The board cannot reduce a bill for hardship or because the value rose from last year.
  • A losing petitioner may sue in circuit court under section 194.171.

The Clerk of the board mails the record of decision within 20 days after the board rules. The appraiser notes that millage is set by the county, cities, school board and water management districts, so neither the board nor the appraiser can change a rate. A household that cannot meet an increase may qualify for a deferral or the installment plan through the tax collector.

sections.h2: What happens if Highlands County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
An unpaid Highlands County account goes to a tax certificate sale on or before June 1, after the newspaper advertisements. A certificate holder may apply for a tax deed once the certificate is two years past the date of delinquency and before seven years from its original issue.

The tax collector says the applicant earns 1.5 percent a month from the month after the application until the account is redeemed or sold, and that the applicant is not guaranteed the property. The Highlands County Clerk of Courts schedules and runs the sale. Statewide rules add that a homestead parcel with under $250 due is issued to the county instead of auctioned, and that the opening bid on homestead property includes half of the latest assessed value.

A seller facing a certificate can still close. Payoff from proceeds redeems the lien before a deed application is filed.

sections.h2: How should you handle Highlands County property tax when selling?
sections.html:
Order a payoff figure before listing, and decide whether the bill has been issued for the year. The tax collector bills the owner of record, and the appraiser's roll is what shows the new owner after a deed is recorded.

The appraiser's database does not hold items such as special assessments for solid waste collection or fire and road improvement districts, though they appear on the tax bill. Ask the tax collector for the complete bill, including non-ad valorem charges, rather than relying on the property record alone. If you are selling a split lot or combining parcels, the appraiser says a survey is needed to split, all taxes on the parcels must be paid, and a mortgage holder must approve in writing.

The state's documentary stamp tax on a deed is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and a change of ownership resets the capped assessment to just value the following January 1. For a current millage figure, check the TRIM notice or ask the appraiser.

faqs.q: When is Highlands County property tax due?
faqs.a: The full bill is due by March 31, and unpaid accounts become delinquent April 1. Bills are mailed October 31, with discounts of 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February.

faqs.q: How do I join the Highlands County installment plan?
faqs.a: Apply with the tax collector by April 30 for the following tax year. Payments are due in June, September, December and March, with discounts of 6%, 4.5% and 3% on the first three, and nothing on the last.

faqs.q: What is the filing deadline for a Highlands County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: March 1, filed with the Highlands County Property Appraiser. The exemption is free to qualified owners, and the office advises ignoring paid mailers that offer to reduce taxable value for a fee.

faqs.q: Can I petition the Value Adjustment Board in Highlands County?
faqs.a: Yes, before the deadline on your TRIM notice. The petition is notarized and costs $50 per parcel, and hardship or a rise in value from last year does not alone support a reduction.

faqs.q: Who runs the Highlands County tax deed sale?
faqs.a: The Clerk of Courts schedules and conducts the sale. A certificate holder applies through the tax collector's vendor after two years from the date of delinquency, and the holder is not guaranteed to obtain the property.
